volkerSchmid.position: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt (DLR)
volkerSchmid.talkTitle: The ISS Missions of Alexander Gerst and Matthias Maurer and Their Societal Relevance
content: In 1998, the first module of the International Space Station (ISS) was launched. The largest project in human spaceflight initially progressed slowly and faced strong criticism, especially in Europe and Germany, where many questioned its cost-benefit ratio.
Following the Space Shuttle Columbia disaster in 2003, European contributions were delayed until 2008.
Thomas Reiter became the first German ESA astronaut on the ISS. Although the first German experiment took place in 2001, full utilization only began in 2011 with a permanent six-person crew.

In 2014, Alexander Gerst spent six months aboard the ISS. His "Blue Dot" mission created widespread public interest in Germany, which continued during his second mission in 2018, when he served as commander.
In 2021, Matthias Maurer became the fourth German astronaut on the ISS and the 600th human in space.

Germany is the largest European stakeholder in the ISS. This raises key questions: Do we benefit from it, or are we only contributing financially? How does logistics work? How are experiments transported to space? What does everyday life on the ISS look like, and what challenges arise?
This talk explores the history, present, and future of the ISS, highlighting its results and wide range of applications through the missions of Gerst and Maurer.

It also explains the complex global cooperation behind the ISS, supported by real mission insights, images, and anecdotes. Selected experiments demonstrate the immense future potential of low Earth orbit as an emerging economic space.

Additionally, the talk addresses the societal relevance of ISS missions, key scientific outcomes, and the cost-benefit relationship. It offers a behind-the-scenes perspective, from the teams planning, preparing, and executing these missions.

Finally, the ISS is presented as a testing ground for long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars. With its planned deorbit in 2031, the talk concludes with an outlook on the future of human space exploration and its continued importance for Earth.

holgerKrag.position: Head of Space Safety Programme Office, ESA
content: Holger Krag is Head of the Space Safety Programme Office at the European Space Agency, where he leads Europe's efforts to ensure safe and sustainable operations in space.
He holds a Master's degree in Aerospace Engineering from the Technical University of Braunschweig and began his career with research focused on space debris modelling and surveillance.
In 2002, he joined Thales ATM in Germany and contributed to the development of the Galileo Ground Mission Segment, including validation systems, working closely with international teams in France.

Since joining ESA in 2006, he has played a key role in developing space debris risk models, collision avoidance systems, and early space surveillance capabilities. In 2014, he became Head of the Space Debris Office, supporting ESA's Space Situational Awareness Programme.
In 2019, he took over leadership of the Space Safety Programme, expanding its scope to include:
Space debris monitoring and mitigation.
Space weather forecasting.
Planetary defence.
The programme includes major missions such as Lagrange, Hera, and ADRIOS, aimed at protecting Earth and space infrastructure.
His responsibilities include defining programme strategy, coordinating with international partners, managing resources and contracts, and representing ESA globally on space safety matters.
Through his work, Holger Krag contributes to shaping the future of space as a secure, sustainable, and operational environment for science, industry, and society.

michaelBoss.position: Chief Commercial Officer Europa, Starlab Space GmbH
michaelBoss.talkTitle: Strategic access to space and microgravity: from Artemis 2 and the Moon to Starlab and commercial LEO
content: This presentation highlights Airbus's contribution in Germany to international collaborations within the current era of human spaceflight—from the return to the Moon to the establishment of a permanent commercial infrastructure in Earth orbit.

Artemis 2: The return to the Moon begins in Bremen. The first part covers Airbus Bremen's crucial role in the Artemis 2 mission, centered on the European Service Module (ESM), the technological heart of the Orion spacecraft. Beyond an overview of the overall system and lunar orbit—including perspectives often summarized in outreach as the "dark side" of the Moon—the talk stresses how international cooperation is essential to mission success.

Starlab: a next-generation space station. The transition from the International Space Station to NASA's Commercial LEO Destination (CLD) program marks a paradigm shift. The presentation introduces the Starlab joint venture between Voyager Technologies, Mitsubishi Corporation, and Airbus. With a planned service life of more than 30 years, Starlab is a next-generation platform that secures Europe's strategic access to the microgravity environment and our contribution to the global LEO economy. The emerging LEO ecosystem offers opportunities especially for students, academia, institutions and agencies, startups, and SMEs.
Momentum Aerospace will provide an industry perspective as a young startup operating in Germany's aerospace sector.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: The protection of your personal data is very important to us. This Privacy Policy informs you about the type, scope, and purpose of the collection and use of personal data on the website of the BVSR Conference 2026, organized by TU Darmstadt Space Technology e.V. (TUDSaT).
privacy.p1: We only collect and process personal data that you voluntarily provide to us, for example, when contacting us via email or filling out forms (e.g., sponsorship form). Typical data may include your name, email address, company, and message.
privacy.p2: The personal data provided will be used solely for purposes related to the organization and execution of the BVSR Conference 2026 Conference, including responding to inquiries, coordinating sponsorships, and providing updates.
privacy.p3: We do not pass on your personal data to third parties without your explicit consent, unless we are legally obliged to do so.
privacy.p4: Our website may use cookies and server log files to ensure functionality and security. These do not allow direct conclusions about your personal identity.
privacy.p5: You have the right to request information about the data stored about you, its origin and recipient, as well as the purpose of storage. You also have the right to request correction, blocking, or deletion of your data.
privacy.p6: For questions regarding data protection, please contact us at:

sponsors.heroLead: The BVSR Conference is made possible through the support of industry, research institutions, and partner organizations. Thank you to everyone helping us grow the student space community in Germany.
sponsors.supportersIntro: We are grateful for the organizations backing BVSR 2026.
sponsors.programP1: The BVSR Conference is an annual event that brings together space enthusiasts from all over Germany. Both size and impact of this conference are growing steadily from year to year, which also increases the financial resources required. Therefore, we highly appreciate your interest in helping us organize this conference. Your influence can take various forms, which are explained in more detail below:
sponsors.programNote: Please also understand that this catalog is not yet final and we reserve the right to make changes. Should this be the case, we will of course consult with you to find a satisfactory solution.
sponsors.donationsP1: If you would like to make a monetary or in-kind donation outside of the packages listed below, simply get in touch with us. We are grateful for your help! As a token of our gratitude, we usually list all our supporters on our conference website and publish a social media post containing all supporters. If requested, we will happily issue a donation receipt. You will also be explicitly invited to participate in the forum of academic spaceflight.
sponsors.sponsoringP1: The conference sponsorship packages are divided into three categories. Each package opens up new opportunities for you and your company to participate in the BVSR conference and its potential benefits. We are open to your personal suggestions and requests in order to put together a package that suits you as well as possible.

sponsors.extraWorkshopText: Organization of a two-hour workshop for approximately 5–20 members of the BVSR on a topic of your choice. We are happy to work with you to develop ideas that will appeal to as many interested individuals as possible.
